sum: A 13-day traverse: up the Langtang valley to Kyanjin Gompa, across to the Gosaikunda lakes, over the Laurebina La and down the Helambu ridge to Sundarijal.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, though checks on the trail are inconsistent. On this route the guide matters most between Gosaikunda and Tharepati, where the path is easy to lose in snow or cloud and there are few lodges and fewer people. They will also know which roadhead is in use since the 2026 flood.

access: By road to the start, and a short drive home from the finish. The classic start is Syabrubesi, seven to nine hours by bus or jeep from Machhapokhari in Kathmandu. Since the Bhote Koshi flood of August 2026 cut that road, groups have been starting from Dhunche or Thulo Syabru and joining the valley trail near Bamboo. The trek ends at Sundarijal, under an hour from Thamel.

photo.a: Layer upon layer of blue ridges fades into haze under an orange dawn sky, with a snow-dusted rocky ridge in the right foreground.
photo.c: Dawn over the foothills, Langtang National Park

includes: porter with most agencies (an extra with some)
Langtang and Shivapuri park permits and TIMS card
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

permits.name: Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park entry ticket
permits.fee: NPR 1,000 per person, per day and entry
permits.where: At the park gate, for example at Sundarijal.

transportText: Bus or a jeep seat from Kathmandu to the Langtang roadhead, and a taxi shared by two back from Sundarijal
tips: Keep a spare day in hand for the pass. Weather that closes the Laurebina La often clears within a day or two.
Carry microspikes from November to April for the traverse to the lake and the far side of the pass.
Bring cash for the whole trek from Kathmandu, including the Shivapuri Nagarjun National Park ticket you need on the last day.
Pack for both ends of the scale: nights below freezing at Kyanjin Gompa and the lake, and warm, humid afternoons on the final ridge.
Trekking poles are worth their weight here. The route has several descents of 1,000 m or more.

days.note: The Pasang Lhamu Highway through Trishuli Bazaar and Dhunche, where park permits are checked. With the road cut short of Syabrubesi since the August 2026 flood, expect to start from Dhunche or Thulo Syabru instead and adjust the next day to suit.

Into the gorge of the Langtang Khola: shady forest, a rising trail and the river loud beside you all day. Bamboo is the natural lunch stop. Keep something in reserve for the last steep pull to Rimche and Lama Hotel. Starting from Thulo Syabru, you join the trail just below Bamboo.

The forest thins at Ghodatabela, where permits are checked, and the valley opens into pasture with Langtang Lirung ahead. The sleeping height rises by 960 m, so drink plenty and keep the pace gentle; Thangshyap is the fallback if you feel it. The rebuilt village lies just past the 2015 debris.
A half day through Mundu and across old moraine to the last settlement in the valley. Use the afternoon for a slow walk around the gompa and the cheese factory, and an early night.

days.t: Kyanjin Ri and a second night at Kyanjin Gompa
days.note: Climb the ridge behind the lodges to 4,773 m for the view over the Lirung glacier, and be down for lunch. This is the acclimatization that the Gosaikunda section depends on, so do not skip it to save a day. Strong walkers can take the longer day on Tserko Ri instead.
Back down the valley in one long, mostly downhill day. The thicker air is welcome; the pounding on your knees is not. Stop at Rimche if Lama Hotel is full.

Follow the gorge down past Bamboo, then leave the Syabrubesi trail at the signed junction and cross a side valley to Thulo Syabru. The final climb to the village is steep and comes at the end of a long downhill morning. The slopes here slide in the monsoon; ask at Bamboo about the state of the path.

A steady 1,100 m climb from the top of the village through oak, hemlock and rhododendron, past the teahouses at Dursagang and along the Foprang Danda ridge to Chandanbari. The gain is large, but you have already slept at 3,870 m, so it is hard work rather than an altitude risk.
why: A climb of 1,120 m in one day, to sleep at 3,330 m. Go slowly, drink plenty, and say so if you get a headache.

days.note: Out of the forest at Cholangpati and up the open ridge to Laurebina, then a narrow traverse above Saraswati Kunda and Bhairav Kunda to the main lake. It is another 1,050 m of sleeping height. Most people manage it after Kyanjin Gompa; if you have any doubt, stop at Laurebina.
why: Sleeping altitude rises 1,050 m in one day, well over the 500 m guideline. Split the climb if you can.
About 1,400 m gained above 3,000 m without a rest night.

days.t: Over the Laurebina La to Ghopte
days.note: The hardest day. An hour and a half past small lakes to the 4,610 m pass, a long, rocky descent to the lodges at Phedi, then three tiring hours in and out of ravines to Ghopte. There is no shelter between the lake and Phedi. Start at first light, and do not cross in fresh snow or thick cloud.

More ravines and a final climb bring you onto the ridge at Tharepati in about two hours, where you join the Helambu circuit. Ignore the branch that drops east to Melamchi Gaun and follow the ridge south, down through forest past Magin Goth to Kutumsang, where the park checkpost looks at permits.

Down the ridge through Tamang farmland: Golphu Bhanjyang, a forested shoulder, the stone steps below Chipling and the saddle at Pati Bhanjyang, then a final 400 m climb to Chisapani. Dirt roads cross the trail repeatedly, so keep asking for the footpath.

n: Hotel Trekkers paradise and Mountain View Restaurant

days.t: Chisapani to Sundarijal, drive to Kathmandu
days.note: Watch the sunrise, then climb for an hour to the Borlang Bhanjyang saddle and descend through the Shivapuri forest and Mulkharka to the road at Sundarijal. A taxi or local bus has you in Thamel in under an hour.
